source_text: Nunc autem, cum Apostolus non solum non postposuerit culpae gratiam, verum etiam praeposuerit dicens multo in plures abundasse beneficia quam irrepsisse dispendia, per opinionem autem traducis multo magis constet nocuisse peccata quam profuisse gratiam, irrefutabiliter approbatum est apostolum Paulum nihil sensisse de traduce, sed eius sententia Traducianos cum Manichaeis magistris suis pariter fuisse destructos.
pass_a_gloss: But now, when the Apostle not only did not postpone grace to fault, but even set it before, saying that benefits abounded much unto more than losses crept in, but through the opinion of the tradux it stands much more that sins harmed than grace helped, it has been irrefutably approved that the apostle Paul meant nothing about the tradux, but that by his sentence the Traduciani together with their Manichaean teachers were equally destroyed.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Traduciani=those who teach tradux peccati; not merely traducianism of the soul
LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: Now, however, the apostle not only did not rank grace below the fault; he ranked it above, saying that benefits abounded to far more people than losses had crept into (Romans 5:15). Under the theory of inherited transmission, by contrast, sins clearly did far more harm than grace did good. It has therefore been irrefutably proved that the apostle Paul meant nothing about inherited transmission; rather, his statement destroyed its advocates together with their Manichaean teachers.

choices.why: Julian's label for teachers of tradux peccati. Keep the polemic name as a description of transmitted sin, not as a theory of the soul's origin.
Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)
